ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To burn a finger is literal bodily burning; the selected sources place it in distinct pleas, austerity lists, and disciplinary lists.
EvidenceBody: In Fu Dashi’s record, petitioners say they cut their ears and burn fingers while urgently pressing a request. The Records of Returning All Good lists finger burning beside burning the body and arm as austerities; the Admonitions text lists it beside burning incense in a legal or disciplinary sequence. Only the first witness ties it to that plea, so no single vow, offering, or institutional purpose is projected across all three.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Chan institutional and documentary prose preserves literal finger burning among costly public religious acts.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The rows differ between a narrated plea and prescriptive lists; none licenses treating every case as the same vow.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: All witnesses denote the same physical injury. Plea, austerity, and disciplinary-list settings are distinct deployments, not separate referents or a license to infer one universal vow function.
